hypotheses.text: Protein-truncating variants (PTVs) in MSL2 cause neurodevelopmental disease primarily through haploinsufficiency, exhibiting phenotypic severity and core feature penetrance (global developmental delay, hypotonia, and facial dysmorphisms) equivalent to, rather than significantly more severe than, pathogenic domain-specific missense variants.
hypotheses.rationale: In chromatin-modifying complexes, loss-of-function alleles often define the baseline haploinsufficiency phenotype. Karayol et al. described 25 individuals with both missense and PTVs showing shared core phenotypes, reduced MSL2 expression in patient iPSCs, and a shared specific episignature, suggesting a unified loss-of-function/haploinsufficiency mechanism rather than an aggravated phenotype for PTVs.

evidence.text: Karayol et al. evaluated 25 individuals harboring either heterozygous missense or protein-truncating alleles in MSL2, identifying common core phenotypes across both classes including developmental delay, hypotonia, motor and speech coordination issues, and a uniform DNA methylation episignature, with patient-derived iPSCs demonstrating reduced MSL2 protein levels across tested variants.

hypotheses.text: Truncating variants that localize to the terminal exon of MSL2 escape nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) and confer a distinct, more severe syndromic presentation involving congenital structural brain anomalies (such as ventriculomegaly) relative to early truncating variants.
hypotheses.rationale: Torene et al. systematically identified MSL2 as carrying de novo PTVs in the NMD-escape region (PTVescs) in NDD cohorts, and Zgheib et al. reported prenatal ventriculomegaly associated with a frameshift/splice alteration in MSL2. Escaping NMD can yield stable truncated dominant-negative proteins that impair the MSL complex more disruptively than simple heterozygous loss.

evidence.text: Torene et al. highlighted MSL2 among genes significantly enriched for de novo protein-truncating variants occurring within the terminal region that escape nonsense-mediated decay (PTVescs) in a cohort of 29,031 NDD trios.

source.title: Prenatal Diagnosis of MSL2‐Related Ventriculomegaly in Association With an Inherited 15q13 Microduplication
source.quote: The fetus, who presented with bilateral moderate ventriculomegaly, also carried a paternally inherited 15q13 microduplication. Brain MRI at 2 and 4 months of age showed stable, mildly enlarged lateral ventricles. Clinical evaluation at 11 months revealed only a mild developmental delay.

hypotheses.text: Epileptic seizures and severe motor coordination impairment are not restricted to or enriched in truncating MSL2 variant carriers compared to individuals harboring missense variants.
hypotheses.rationale: Karayol et al. established epilepsy and coordination difficulties as key phenotypic facets across their mixed 25-individual cohort of missense and PTV carriers, suggesting neurological excitability and cerebellar/motor pathway impairment stem from general MSL2 dose reduction rather than severe PTV-exclusive mechanisms.

evidence.text: In a combined cohort of 25 individuals with heterozygous missense or protein-truncating alleles, Karayol et al. reported coordination problems, motor issues, and seizures as part of the unified phenotypic spectrum without segregation to truncating alleles.

new_directions.question_text: Do truncating variants and RING- or CXC-domain missense variants in MSL2 induce distinct peripheral blood DNA methylation episignatures?
new_directions.rationale: Karayol et al. defined a sensitive and specific episignature for MSL2 variants; determining whether sub-episignatures partition PTVs from functional domain missense variants will definitively clarify whether their downstream epigenomic impact differs in severity.

new_directions.question_text: What is the penetrance and severity of structural central nervous system anomalies (e.g. ventriculomegaly) in PTV versus missense variant carriers across all published MSL2 cases?
new_directions.rationale: Zgheib et al. reported prenatal ventriculomegaly with an MSL2 truncating/splice defect; quantifying brain imaging abnormalities between PTV and missense cohorts will help determine if brain dysmorphology is variant-type specific.
